chapter_name: HOT Category Puzzles – Uncertain Seating Arrangement Based

questions.question_text:
An unknown-length straight row faces south. Q is sixth to the right of S; T is fourth to the left of Q; two people sit between Q and P; six sit between W and V; R is fourth to the left of S; U sits between S and T; V is second to the right of U; W is third from an end; S is eighth from the left end (read relative to the facing direction, as reflected by the source solution diagram).

Question: How many persons are sitting in the row?
questions.explanation: Exhaustive placement with south-facing left/right gives one row length, 20. The named seats are W=3, P=4, Q=7, V=10, T=11, U=12, S=13 and R=17; all stated offsets hold.
questions.source: PDF: HOT Category Puzzles Uncertain Seating Arrangement based 01 _ Class Notes.pdf; physical page(s) 8-10

questions.question_text:
An unknown-length north-facing row. M is eighth left of J; N is fourth right of K; O immediately left of P; L is exactly midway between K and J; P is third from the right end. The number between J and P equals that between K and J. Exactly ten people are left of J; six people are between N and O; the number between M and J equals that between Q and J.

Question: How many persons are sitting in the row?
questions.explanation: J has exactly ten people to its left, so J=11. The K/J gap equals the J/P gap; the midpoint clue puts L midway between K and J. The K=17 branch would force P=17 too, so it collides; thus K=5,L=8. P is six positions right of J at 17, so n=19. O=P−1=16, N=K+4=9, and six people lie between N and O. M=3 and Q=19 satisfy the final equal-gap clue.
questions.source: PDF: HOT Category Puzzles Uncertain Seating Arrangement based 01 _ Class Notes.pdf; physical page(s) 11-13

questions.question_text:
A straight row of an unknown number of people faces south. W is fifth to the left of U; two people sit between W and X; X is second from an end; five people sit between X and V; S is eighth to the right of V; the number between U and S equals the number between T and S; exactly two people sit to T’s right.

Question: Who is sitting second to the left of U?
questions.explanation: Constraint enumeration yields one valid row of 24 seats: T=3, S=9, U=15, V=17, W=20, X=23. For south-facing people, second to U’s left is two physical positions to the right of U, position 17, occupied by V.
questions.source: PDF: HOT Category Puzzles Uncertain Seating Arrangement based 01 _ Class Notes.pdf; physical page(s) 14-16

questions.question_text:
An unknown-length north-facing row. G is third to either side of H. B is sixth left of C, and C is second left of E. G and E are immediate neighbors of D. F is fourth right of H. The number between H and A is one less than the number between B and C. I is immediately left of H, and the number to the left of I is twice the number between B and E. A is second from the right end.

Question: How many persons are sitting in the row?
questions.explanation: The written clues force I=15 and H=16; A must be 21, hence n=22. A satisfying placement is B3,C9,E11,D12,G13,H16,F20,A21,I15. The count 22 is not among 20,19,23,18, so option E is correct.
questions.source: PDF: HOT Category Puzzles Uncertain Seating Arrangement based 02 _ Class Notes.pdf.pdf; physical page(s) 4-6

questions.question_text:
An unknown row of fewer than 20 people, facing north. Q is fifth right of R. J is third left of U and adjacent to Q; P sits exactly midway between Q and U. The number between R and M equals the number between B and R. The number between M and B equals the number between B and U. Six people sit between P and L, with L at an end. The number right of G equals the number left of M.

Question: How many persons sit in the row?

options.A: Twice the number to the right of Q
options.B: Thrice the number between R and P

questions.explanation: Exhaustive enumeration gives one arrangement with n=19: M2,R5,B8,Q10,J11,P12,U14,G18,L19. Both relational distractors evaluate to 18, while the row contains 19 people; option C is the only correct choice.
questions.source: PDF: HOT Category Puzzles Uncertain Seating Arrangement based 02 _ Class Notes.pdf.pdf; physical page(s) 7-9

questions.question_text:
An unknown-length north-facing row of at least 20 people. Three sit between W and G and neither is at an end. Y is second right of G. The number between W and G is one more than the number between Y and C, with C right of W. B is fourth right of C; R is third left of W. The number left of R is one less than the number between G and Y. Two sit between B and M, which is not adjacent to C. The number right of M is one less than the number left of W.

Question: What is the position of Y with respect to W?
questions.explanation: The clues force W=4, R=1, G=8 and Y=10. The Y-to-W offset is +6 in the north-facing row, so option A. Full solution: R1,W4,C13,G8,Y10,B17,M20, row length 22.
questions.source: PDF: HOT Category Puzzles Uncertain Seating Arrangement based 02 _ Class Notes.pdf.pdf; physical page(s) 10-12

questions.question_text:
Shared directions: An unknown number of people in a north-facing row. R is third right of M. Three people sit between S and R. The number between M and S is one less than the number between M and G; G is left of M. S is third left of Q. Q is fifth left of L at an end. The number right of Q is one less than the number left of G. P is at the left end, and more than ten people sit between P and M.

Question: Which of the following statements is true? I. G sits to the left of R. II. More than seven persons sit between M and S. III. Not more than two persons sit between S and Q. IV. R sits exactly midway between M and S.
questions.explanation: The unique row has P1,G7,M15,R18,S22,Q25,L30 (n=30). I is true; II is false because six people are between M and S; III is true because two people are between S and Q; IV is false because R=18 is not the midpoint of 15 and 22.
questions.source: PDF: HOT Category Puzzles Uncertain Seating Arrangement based 03  Class Notes.pdf; physical page(s) 8-10

questions.question_text:
Shared directions: An unknown north-facing row. H is at the leftmost seat; two people sit between H and L; M neighbors L. K is fourth left of I. The number between L and K is one less than the number between I and K. O is exactly midway between I and K. More than three people sit between M and O; O is fifth from the right end.

Question: How many persons are sitting in the row?
questions.explanation: H=1 and L=4. K cannot be 1 because H is there, so K=7; I=11 and O=9. M must be the other neighbor of L, position 3: M=5 would leave only three people between M and O, not more than three. O fifth from the right gives n=13.
questions.source: PDF: HOT Category Puzzles Uncertain Seating Arrangement based 03  Class Notes.pdf; physical page(s) 11-12

questions.question_text:
An unknown north-facing row. N is fourth left of Q; two sit between Q and L; the number between N/L equals the number between L/P. P is fourth right of S. The number between S/P is one more than that between M/N; M and P are not neighbors. I is immediately left of S; no more than five people sit right of I. The number right of I is one more than the number left of G. G is second left of M; three sit between G and T. T is not adjacent to Q or N; more than two sit between T and N.

Question: How many persons are sitting in the row?
questions.explanation: The written equations force N=10,Q=14,L=17,P=24,S=20,I=19,G=5,M=7 and T=2. The row therefore has 24 seats. Exhaustive enumeration gives one valid placement; the visible answer mark B agrees.
questions.source: PDF: HOT Category Puzzles Uncertain Seating Arrangement based 04 _ Class Notes.pdf.pdf; physical page(s) 7-8

questions.question_text:
An unknown north-facing row. Three people sit between A and B; C is second right of A; three sit between B and D; E is immediately left of A; C is fifth from the right end; I is at an end. The number between C and F equals the number between F and D. J is second left of G, which is adjacent to B; no more than two people sit between G and D. Five sit between D and I; H is midway between D and I.

Question: Who is sitting second to the right of G?
questions.explanation: Exhaustive enumeration produces one valid 21-seat row: I1,H4,D7,J8,G10,B11,F12,E14,A15,C17. The second seat right of G (10) is position 12, occupied by F; option A.
questions.source: PDF: HOT Category Puzzles Uncertain Seating Arrangement based 04 _ Class Notes.pdf.pdf; physical page(s) 13-15

questions.question_text:
An unknown south-facing row. C is at an end. The number between D and F equals the number between E and D. Eight people sit between E and B; one person sits between C and E. B is third from an end. A is fifth to the right of D (relative to south-facing people). More than six sit between C and F; no more than five sit between B and A.

Question: How many persons are sitting in the row?
questions.explanation: Exhaustive enumeration gives one 14-seat row: B3,A4,F6,D9,E12,C14. For a south-facing person, right is physical left, so A=D−5. Every distance clue is satisfied; option D.
questions.source: PDF: HOT Category Puzzles Uncertain Seating Arrangement based 04 _ Class Notes.pdf.pdf; physical page(s) 16-18
